Jobs, fellowships, courses and calls

University of Zurich seeks a professor of the cultural history of India

The open-rank post, described as premodern Indology with the specialisation left open, is at the Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies. It starts on 1 August 2028 and closes to applications on 7 December 2026.

Talaash Heritage desk · Published 5 November 2026

Where
Zurich, Switzerland
Apply by
7 December 2026

The University of Zurich is advertising a full-time professorship in the Cultural History of India at its Institute of Asian and Oriental Studies, in the Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences. The post is open rank: depending on the appointee's record it will be a full or associate professorship, or an assistant professorship with tenure track. It begins on 1 August 2028.

Applicants need a doctorate in Indology or a related discipline, completed by the time they apply, along with further strong publications and internationally visible research on the cultural history of India. The university asks for source-based work on India's intellectual, religious and artistic traditions and their reception, drawn from texts, material evidence or both.

Language is central to the post. Candidates must be able to read and analyse sources closely in at least one Indian language, and the university would prefer someone who has both a classical language and a modern one such as Hindi, Bengali, Tamil or Urdu. Scholars from neighbouring fields, including religious studies, history, art history, anthropology, linguistics and legal history, are welcome if their research rests on archives and texts and they show competence in Indian languages.

Teaching will range widely across texts, images and objects, taking in religious life and ritual, art, law, politics, society and gender. The post also involves working with the social-science chair in Indian Studies and with the Museum Rietberg and the university's Ethnographic Museum.

Teaching may be in English, but non-German speakers must gain a working knowledge of German within three years. Applications are made online through the university's jobs portal by 7 December 2026.
